<a name="TopicACPPermissionRequested"></a>TopicACPPermissionRequested fires when a permission\_mode "human" \(or decision\-lane escalated\) session/requestPermission enters the pending registry. TopicACPPermissionResolved fires when the wait terminates \(answered, timeout, or fail\-closed rejections\). Typed Topic\[T\] per internal/comm/AGENTS.md: the payload is stable and single\-shape.

	var (
	    TopicACPPermissionRequested = NewTopic[ACPPermissionEvent]("acp.permission.requested")
	    TopicACPPermissionResolved  = NewTopic[ACPPermissionEvent]("acp.permission.resolved")
	)

<a name="ErrBusClosed"></a>ErrBusClosed is returned by the blocking publish paths when the bus has been shut down: a critical event can never be delivered after Close, and the caller must terminalize honestly instead of hanging on the 5s bound.

	var ErrBusClosed = errors.New("bus: message bus closed")

<a name="ErrLoopClosed"></a>ErrLoopClosed is the closed\-runtime sentinel for turn submission: a turn handed to a torn\-down loop must terminalize failed with this error instead of running on dead state or vanishing silently. The closed\-loop guard itself \(RunOnceWithParts check \+ stale\-loop rebuild\) is 01\-safety/05 T4; this leaf declares the shared sentinel so the turn outbox and the guard agree on the error identity.

	var ErrLoopClosed = errors.New("agent: loop closed")

	func IsCriticalTopic(topic string) bool

IsCriticalTopic reports whether topic is in the C6 critical set: a per\-task/plan\-once terminal event that must use the blocking publish path and is exempt from the poll buffer's drop\-oldest trim.

	func MatchWildcard(pattern, topic string) bool

MatchWildcard is the exported form of the bus's topic matcher. The TUI's topic\-overlap guard previously tested a hand\-rolled MIRROR of this function, so a semantics change here left the guard green while the daemon double\-delivered \(bughunt LOW\); consumers must test against this.

<a name="PublishBlockingT"></a>
## func PublishBlockingT

	func PublishBlockingT[T any](b *MessageBus, t Topic[T], source string, payload T) int

PublishBlockingT is PublishT with MessageBus.PublishBlocking delivery: sends to subscriber channels with a 5\-second timeout instead of a non\-blocking drop\-on\-full. For per\-turn\-once events whose loss breaks a client state machine \(turn.terminal is the canonical case: awaiting clients key on it, and the C\-09 security\-approval class of full\-buffer drops applies\). Marshal policy identical to PublishT.

<a name="PublishT"></a>
## func PublishT

	func PublishT[T any](b *MessageBus, t Topic[T], source string, payload T) int

PublishT marshals payload as T and publishes to t's topic.

Marshal\-failure policy: json.Marshal of T fails only for channels, funcs, or reference cycles \- programmer error, not a runtime condition. This library therefore PANICS with a wrapped, descriptive message on marshal failure \(option \(a\)\); repo precedent for panicking on programmer\-error conditions exists in internal/llm, internal/security, and internal/auth, and no precedent prohibits it in bus\-adjacent code. The returned int is the delivery count from MessageBus.Publish.

<a name="ACPPermissionEvent"></a>
## type ACPPermissionEvent

ACPPermissionEvent is the frozen bus/WS payload for the human permission relay \(acp\-human\-permission\-relay leaf 03, Contract C\). The daemon\-side notifier \(internal/daemon/acp\_notifier.go\) adapts the internal/acp PendingPermission value into this shape and publishes it on TopicACPPermissionRequested / TopicACPPermissionResolved.

The payload lives in internal/bus — NOT internal/acp — so HTTP/WS/TUI/GUI consumers can decode it without pulling the ACP client into their dependency closure \(internal/acp must not gain a bus dep; the daemon does the adaptation, per the leaf's import\-cycle note\). wsclass imports nothing from internal/, so bus \-\> wsclass is cycle\-free \(same direction as agent \-\> wsclass\).

Wire keys are frozen \(leaf 03 task 1\): id, agent\_id, session\_id, summary, created\_at \(\+ decision/reason on the resolved frame\). Options is the additive acp\-always\-allow key \(leaf 01\): present on frames whose agent offered options, omitted otherwise — old consumers decode by key and are unaffected. Persona is likewise additive \(permission surfaces phase 2\): the multi\-session persona that asked, omitted on the no\-persona lane so old\-frame publishers keep their exact prior wire shape.

	type ACPPermissionEvent struct {
	    ID        string `json:"id"`
	    AgentID   string `json:"agent_id"`
	    Persona   string `json:"persona,omitempty"`
	    SessionID string `json:"session_id"`
	    Summary   string `json:"summary"`
	    CreatedAt string `json:"created_at"` // RFC3339 stamp of registration
	    // Options are the agent-offered permission options (raw labels),
	    // bounded by the relay at register time (omitted when none).
	    Options []ACPPermissionOption `json:"options,omitempty"`
	    // Decision + Reason are empty on the requested frame and carry the
	    // terminal answer ("allow"/"always"/"deny", "answered"/"timeout"/
	    // "no_relay"/"full") on the resolved frame.
	    Decision string `json:"decision,omitempty"`
	    Reason   string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	    // Approver identifies WHO answered (audit M5 attribution): the
	    // rendered acp.Approver ("peercred:pid=…,uid=…", "http-key:<sha256
	    // prefix>", "in-process"). Empty on the requested frame and on
	    // timeout/no-relay resolutions; never carries raw credentials.
	    // Additive like Options — old consumers decode by key and are
	    // unaffected.
	    Approver string `json:"approver,omitempty"`
	}

<a name="MessageBus.HasSubscribers"></a>
### func \(\*MessageBus\) HasSubscribers

	func (b *MessageBus) HasSubscribers(topic string) bool

HasSubscribers reports whether any subscriber \(direct or wildcard\) is registered for the given topic. Use this to skip expensive publishes when nobody is listening \(e.g., SSE heartbeats in non\-streaming mode\).

<a name="MessageBus.Publish"></a>
### func \(\*MessageBus\) Publish

	func (b *MessageBus) Publish(topic string, msg *models.BusMessage) int

Publish sends a message to all subscribers of the topic. It also publishes to wildcard subscribers \(e.g., "agent.\*" matches "agent.status"\). A nil msg is silently dropped to protect subscriber goroutines from nil\-pointer dereferences when reading the message.

<a name="MessageBus.PublishBlocking"></a>
### func \(\*MessageBus\) PublishBlocking

	func (b *MessageBus) PublishBlocking(topic string, msg *models.BusMessage) int

PublishBlocking sends a message to all subscribers, blocking until the message is enqueued in every subscriber's channel or a 5\-second timeout elapses. Use this for security\-critical events where message drops are unacceptable \(e.g., approval requests\). Returns the number of subscribers the message was delivered to.

<a name="MessageBus.PublishBlockingErr"></a>
### func \(\*MessageBus\) PublishBlockingErr

	func (b *MessageBus) PublishBlockingErr(topic string, msg *models.BusMessage) (int, error)

PublishBlockingErr is PublishBlocking with an explicit error result for the C6 critical\-delivery path: it returns ErrBusClosed when the bus is shut down \(before or during the bounded wait\) so producers can terminalize honestly instead of reporting a silent zero delivery. Per\-subscriber timeouts still log at Error and simply do not count as delivered; the bounded\-wait contract \(5s per subscriber\) is unchanged.

<a name="MessageBus.PublishExternalOnly"></a>
### func \(\*MessageBus\) PublishExternalOnly

	func (b *MessageBus) PublishExternalOnly(topic string, msg *models.BusMessage) int

PublishExternalOnly is like Publish but marks the "no subscribers" debug log as an external\-only topic. Use this for fire\-and\-forget event topics that are informational and expected to have no subscriber when no TUI/MCP client is connected \(e.g., worker.\*, chat.message.received\). The panicOnUndrainedSubscription behavior is unchanged — it now logs at Error level instead of panicking, so tests still catch missing wiring.

<a name="MessageBus.SubscribeWithBuffer"></a>
### func \(\*MessageBus\) SubscribeWithBuffer

	func (b *MessageBus) SubscribeWithBuffer(id, topic string, bufferSize int) *Subscriber

SubscribeWithBuffer creates a subscription with an explicit channel capacity, overriding the bus\-wide default BufferSize \(bufferSize \<= 0 falls back to the default\). Callers whose consumers drain slower than burst producers \- e.g. the rpc poll collectors, C6 \- size their own channel so a flood lands in the caller's bounded ring and its explicit drop accounting instead of silently overflowing a default\-capacity channel on the bus side.

<a name="MessageBus.TurnOutbox"></a>
### func \(\*MessageBus\) TurnOutbox

	func (b *MessageBus) TurnOutbox() *TurnOutbox

TurnOutbox returns the bus's terminal\-outbox store, creating it on first use \(capacity DefaultTurnOutboxCapacity\). Nil\-safe. The store is the C6 recovery seam: critical terminals are captured at publish time even when live delivery drops, and the turn.result query RPC \(01\-safety/05 T5\) reads it for disconnected\-client recovery.

<a name="SubscribeT"></a>
### func SubscribeT

	func SubscribeT[T any](b *MessageBus, id string, t Topic[T], fn func(T)) *Subscriber

SubscribeT subscribes to t and invokes fn with each decoded payload.

Decode failures are logged at warn level \(topic \+ type name\) and the message is dropped.

Lifetime: SubscribeT starts exactly ONE reader goroutine that runs until the subscriber's channel is closed \(by MessageBus.Close or Unsubscribe\). Callers must Unsubscribe the returned Subscriber when done, exactly as with the raw Subscribe API.

SubscriptionHandler manages bus subscriptions with automatic lifecycle management. It handles subscribe/dispatch/teardown to eliminate duplicated handler boilerplate.

<a name="TurnOutbox"></a>
## type TurnOutbox

TurnOutbox retains per\-turn\-once terminal outcomes so a client that missed the live event \(full buffer timeout, daemon restart, reconnect\) can always recover the turn outcome \(C6 / W25 recovery seam\). It is bounded drop\-oldest with explicit overflow accounting: retention loss is counted, never silent. Safe for concurrent use.

The turn.result query RPC that exposes this store is 01\-safety/05 T5; this leaf owns the store and the publish\-side capture.

	type TurnOutbox struct {
	    // contains filtered or unexported fields
	}

<a name="NewTurnOutbox"></a>
### func NewTurnOutbox

	func NewTurnOutbox(capacity int) *TurnOutbox

NewTurnOutbox creates an outbox retaining at most capacity terminal outcomes. capacity \<= 0 falls back to DefaultTurnOutboxCapacity.

<a name="TurnOutbox.Lookup"></a>
### func \(\*TurnOutbox\) Lookup

	func (o *TurnOutbox) Lookup(turnID string) (TurnOutboxEntry, bool)

Lookup returns the most recent retained terminal for turnID, or false when the outbox holds none \(never retained or trimmed away\).

<a name="TurnOutbox.Record"></a>
### func \(\*TurnOutbox\) Record

	func (o *TurnOutbox) Record(turnID, sessionID, topic string, payload []byte) bool

Record retains a terminal outcome for turnID. Only C6 critical topics are retained; anything else is ignored \(returns false\) so progress chatter can never evict terminals. The payload is copied: callers may reuse their buffer after Record returns.

<a name="TurnOutbox.Since"></a>
### func \(\*TurnOutbox\) Since

	func (o *TurnOutbox) Since(sinceSeq int64) []TurnOutboxEntry

Since returns retained entries with Seq \> sinceSeq in assignment order \(a fresh slice; callers own it\). sinceSeq == 0 returns everything retained.

Stats reports retention accounting: retained entry count, the next assignment seq \(cursor head\), and entries lost to the bounded trim.
